result.summary: Both N slots pass with novelty 4 and soundness 4. The snapshot holds 0 heads, so the seeds could only be checked against the 5 controls. Slot a covers the skew and up/down asymmetry of minute returns. Its seed 12 is struck automatically because its |rho| with 20-day reversal is 0.87, at or above the 0.8 cutoff. Slot b covers how volume lines up with price. Its seed 9 is struck as a duplicate. It sits at |rho| 0.50 with both the known family and liquidity, which is right on the 0.5 line where the reward disqualifies a factor. Its mechanism is mostly noise in estimating the daily correlation, which grows as trading gets thinner. I checked every operator in source. No seed has a look-ahead, numerical-artifact or broken-definition problem, so nothing else is blocked. Four caveats are noted but do not block: (1) slot a seed 11 sorts stocks into price deciles by back-adjusted Close, which does not remove the tick-size effect it is meant to remove. (2) Slot a seed 6 can show one-day spikes on thin, low-priced stocks, because the quantile can be interpolated between 0 and one tick. (3) Slot b seed 1 mostly reflects the large opening and closing auction bars. (4) Slot b seed 14 flips the whole book with the market state, so its turnover will be high. There are no R groups this round.
